newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: One killed as gunmen attack Pakistan Sunni mosque.
newsitem.headline: One killed as gunmen attack Pakistan Sunni mosque.

text.p: Gunmen attacked a prayer meeting at a Sunni sect mosque on Wednesday in Lahore, capital of Pakistan's central province of Punjab, killing one worshipper and injuring three others, police said.

They said two gunmen sprayed bullets from automatic weapons at the mosque, run by the Sunni militant Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) group, in Lahore's Anarkali market in the afternoon, injuring four men, and drove away by car and motorcycle.
One of the injured men, Hafiz Misbahaur Rehman, who was shot while trying to catch a gunman, died later in hospital, the police said.

The identity of the gunmen was not immediately clear, but the incident seemed to be the latest in a wave of attacks in Punjab blamed on rival militant factions of the majority Sunni and the minority Shi'ite sects of Islam.
Two SSP activists were killed on Monday night in Saray Saddu in southern Punjab after the killing of a Shi'ite state radio official in Bahawalpur, another town in the area.

In the southern port city of Karachi, paramilitary troops patrolled the volatile East District on Wednesday after two people were wounded by gunfire and two vehicles set ablaze, police and witnesses there said.
At least three people were killed overnight in Karachi, raising the toll to 11 in political and sectarian violence in the city since Monday, police sources said.

Activists of the breakaway Haqiqi faction of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) blocked roads and chanted slogans against the rival main MQM faction, accusing it of masterminding Tuesday's attack on the Haqiqi headquarters where two people were killed.
Haqiqi has long feuded with the mainstream MQM, which is now part of Sindh province's coalition government led by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League party.
More than 50 people have been killed in ethnic, political and sectarian violence this year in Karachi, capital of Sindh province, compared to 500 last year and about 2,000 in 1995.
Sectarian violence is rife in Punjab, where the SSP and other Sunni groups are pitted against Shi'ite Moslem factions in a feud that has cost more than 70 lives this year.

Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over Islamic beliefs have often spilled into violence in Pakistan that cost at least 170 lives last year. Shi'ites form about 15 percent of Pakistan's population of more than 130 million but are the majority in neighbouring Iran.
